title: This Penguin Dives 1,850 Feet and Holds Its Breath for 27 Minutes

scenes.text: This penguin dives 1,850 feet deep and holds its breath 27 minutes.
The emperor penguin. That's deeper than the Empire State Building is tall, with 50 times the pressure.
Its heart goes from 70 beats a minute down to just 10.
Its muscles store their own oxygen, and non-essential organs switch off.
The bones are solid, not hollow like other birds, so the crushing pressure can't break them.
27 minutes. 1,850 feet. Then it pops back up, like nothing happened.
scenes.keywords: penguin jumping out of water ice

description:
Emperor penguins are the deepest diving birds on Earth. The record dive reached 565 metres (about 1,850 feet) and the longest recorded dive lasted around 27 minutes.
To manage it, the penguin's heart rate drops from about 70 beats a minute to as low as 10, its muscles rely on oxygen stored in myoglobin, non-essential organs shut down, and solid bones resist the pressure.
How long can you hold your breath? Comment your time below.
first_comment: Most emperor penguin dives are a modest 3 to 6 minutes. The 27-minute record came from a bird that was probably trapped under ice and searching for a way out. What is your breath-hold record?
